summary: service role claim canonicalization mismatch prevents tenant admin impersonation in private deployment
description:
Issue summary: After a recent IdP change, tenant-scoped admin impersonation fails for Asterion customers on their private VPC. The Identity Proxy is returning role assertions but Redwood's RBAC lookup does not map them to tenant admin bindings due to claim canonicalization differences (casing and trailing suffix).

Technical background: Customer uses an on-prem IdP that recently started sending service role assertions in the claim 'serviceRoles' with values like 'TenantAdmin/Finance'. Redwood expects the normalized claim key 'service_roles' and lowercased role names without '/' separators. The mismatch causes the tenant admin lookup to return no bindings and results in 403s for impersonation and certain admin operations.
impact: Customer reports that platform admins cannot impersonate users or perform tenant-scoped admin tasks (user invites, role grants). Affects all admin users for one tenant in their private deployment. Blocking day-to-day operations for Asterion's Platform team. Estimated 12 engineers impacted at customer side.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure IdP to emit service role assertion under claim 'serviceRoles' with value 'TenantAdmin/Finance'.
2) Perform a tenant-scoped admin impersonation request to the Redwood Private Admin API with the IdP-issued assertion exchanged via the identity-proxy.
3) Observe 403 response: 'rbac: no matching role binding for tenant'.
4) Confirm that the raw request headers into the serving runtime include 'x-assertion-serviceRoles: TenantAdmin/Finance'.
expected_behavior: Identity proxy or RBAC layer canonicalizes incoming role assertions into the normalized form used by tenant bindings (e.g., 'tenantadmin:finance' or 'tenant_admin'). Tenant admin impersonation should succeed when a binding exists.
actual_behavior: Requests are denied with 403. RBAC lookup logs show 'no bindings found for claim key service_roles' because the identity-proxy passed 'serviceRoles' and the runtime did not map it.
logs: 2026-02-20T09:13:21Z rbac ERROR lookup failed: claim key 'service_roles' missing (trace=tr-9b3f2e)
2026-02-20T09:13:21Z admin-api WARN impersonation denied uid=alice@asterion.com tenant=asterion-finance reason='no role binding'
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: IdP changed claim key casing and added a namespace separator '/'.

Reproduced locally against staging private image: identity-proxy forwarded raw claim exactly as IdP sent it (serviceRoles). RBAC canonicalization code currently only checks for snake_case 'service_roles' and lowercased values without '/'.
Trace tr-9b3f2e corresponds to customer request sample provided by support (attached).
Config mismatch discovered: customer had customized IdP mapping in their nextIdP release; they intended to keep old claim key but legacy outbound mapper now emits the new format.
workaround: Temporary workaround provided to customer: add a claim remap rule in their IdP (or in the identity-proxy 'claim_mapping' config) to emit 'service_roles' with lowercased, colon-separated values. Support provided sample mapping snippet. This restored admin impersonation for the tenant within ~10 minutes.
resolution:
Engineering patch deployed to identity-proxy v1.3.27 that adds robust claim canonicalization: accepts camelCase, PascalCase, kebab-case and snake_case claim keys, strips trailing slashes, and normalizes separators ('/' and ':' to ':') and lowercases role names. A short migration job was run to re-evaluate cached role-bindings for affected tenants. Patch deployed to customer's private control plane on 2026-02-23. Post-deploy verification: impersonation succeeds and no further 403s reported for the tenant.

Follow-ups: (1) update RBAC docs with canonicalization expectations, (2) include a diagnostic check in the Private Console to show raw incoming claims for tenant owners, (3) add automated test coverage for common claim permutations.
